input.title: Move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 to cover LH-07 failure

options.description: No reaction. TP-1310-04 (8.4 g/t) unloaded from 09:30 to 17:00.
Hold until LH-07 is back at 14:30 (PR-0001 likely case, 5 h). Range 12:30 to 16:30.

LH-11 (lowest-grade 'carguio' stope TP-1250-02, 4.1 g/t) moves to TP-1310-04. Leaves 09:35, arrives 10:35 (1 h ramp move, different level). Covers until LH-07 returns at 14:30, then goes back to 1250-02 by 15:30. Total loss: 32.5 t / 8.78 oz at 1310-04 plus 118.3 t / 15.60 oz at 1250-02.

input.calculation:
Oz = t x g/t / 31.1035. TP-1310-04 plans 300 t over the 10 h productive window (07:00-17:00), so 30 t/h at 8.4 g/t, or 8.10 oz/h. TP-1250-02 plans 200 t over 10 h, so 20 t/h at 4.1 g/t, or 2.64 oz/h.
Rules: LOADER-BACKUP-01 says take the loader from the lowest-grade stope. LOADER-BACKUP-02 says only stopes in phase 'carguio' can give one up, so combined-cycle stopes (1310-05, 1220-01, 1280-02, 1310-07) are excluded. Among the 'carguio' stopes the lowest grade is TP-1250-02 at 4.1 g/t, so LH-11 is the candidate. Next candidates are TP-1250-08 (5.8) and TP-1280-06 (5.5). Both lose more oz per hour and give the same or worse move time, so LH-11 also maximizes net ounces. MOVE-TIME-01: 1250 to 1310 is a different level, so 1 h.
1) Do nothing: 09:30 to 17:00 is 7.5 h. 7.5 x 30 = 225 t. 225 x 8.4 / 31.1035 = 60.77 oz.
2) Wait for repair: 09:30 to 14:30 is 5 h (PR-0001 likely case). 5 x 30 = 150 t. 150 x 8.4 / 31.1035 = 40.51 oz. If the repair runs high (16:30), the loss is 7 h = 210 t = 56.7 oz. At the low case (12:30) it is 3 h = 90 t = 24.3 oz.
3) Reassign LH-11: it leaves 09:35 and arrives 10:35. 1310-04 stays unloaded from 09:30 to 10:35 (1.083 h). That is 32.5 t and 8.78 oz lost. LH-11 loads 10:35 to 14:30 (3.917 h). That is 117.5 t and 31.73 oz protected. LH-07 resumes at 14:30. LH-11 then goes back to 1250-02, arriving 15:30. 1250-02 is unloaded from 09:35 to 15:30 (5.917 h). That is 118.3 t and 15.60 oz lost.
Net protected = 31.73 - 15.60 = 16.13 oz. Total at risk = 8.78 + 15.60 = 24.38 oz and 150.8 t.
Option 3 has the lowest oz at risk (24.4 oz, against 40.5 oz for waiting and 60.8 oz for doing nothing). It trades slightly more tonnes lost (150.8 t, against 150 t for waiting) for far lower ounces lost.
If the repair slips to 16:30, keep LH-11 at 1310-04 until LH-07 is back. The net gain then grows to about 7 h x 8.10 minus the 1250-02 loss.

Pump spare stock is not in the data. The warehouse or CMMS stock should confirm it.
Maintenance crew availability is not in the data. The maintenance supervisor should confirm it.
The 30 t/h and 20 t/h rates are the planned shift tonnes spread evenly over 10 h. Actual rates, face readiness and the ramp route for LH-11 should be confirmed with the shift boss (jefe de guardia).
Not used here: the idle reserve places (e.g. TP-1280-09) cannot be loaded because there is no spare loader.
